Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

It has 19 songs and two short spoken introductions, and the current version is called harbor_glass_bellwether_0614_v3.srt. We are using English subtitles only. I am keeping the title cards out of this file because the venue loads those separately, and the opening card already has a separate delivery slot.

Jo is the subtitle editor, and Jo made the first timing pass after the June 2 rehearsal recording arrived. That recording was 42 minutes long and had the band's lead singer, Nia Vale, speaking between songs. Jo matched the lyrics against the approved sheet, then adjusted the spoken sections by listening to the recording. Jo told me, “I left the audience shouts alone unless they covered a lyric.” That means the file includes the shouted “one more song” before the encore, but it does not include every cheer heard under the final chorus. The rehearsal recording is not the concert mix, so I told Jo not to use it to set the final sound cue points.

I sent the current subtitle file to Leena, the venue projectionist, and asked her to check whether the stage screen will be full-width or whether the two narrow side panels will also be used. I need Leena to answer before Jo settles the line breaks, because the smaller panels allow fewer characters per line. Leena has not confirmed the arrangement yet. If she confirms that only the full-width screen will be used, Jo can keep the longer two-line breaks already in v3. If Leena says the side panels are in use, Jo will need to make a second layout with shorter lines; that is a proposal for the next pass, not work that has happened already. I asked Leena to reply by June 10, since Jo has a separate captioning job on June 11 and 12.

There are a few details in the lyric sheet that need to stay exactly as written. The song “Glass Harbor” is the third song, even though the title sounds like the venue name, and its lyric includes the phrase “we keep the light on.” In “Northbound,” Nia sings “I found my way home” twice, with a short instrumental break between the two lines. The lyric sheet has both lines, but Jo has timed them as separate subtitle cues to match the performance. I also checked the names in the spoken introduction: Nia introduces the touring drummer, Ellis Park, and thanks local opener June Arcade. Ellis uses they/them pronouns in the band's notes. Jo put the names on their own lines because the introduction is quick, and I asked Jo not to shorten June Arcade to “June,” which could sound like a date in the file review notes.

1. The file uses a 24-frame-per-second time base, matching the playback package that venue technician Ravi gave me. Jo checked the first cue against the rehearsal recording at 00:01:12, and I checked the last lyric cue against the end of the encore. The file has no subtitle during the two-second black screen before the first song. Ravi said the playback package accepts SRT files, but he has not tested this particular version on the house system.
2. The house screen is normally set to white text with a thin dark outline. Leena told me that the font size is controlled in the projection system, not in the subtitle file, so Jo did not add styling tags. The band's lighting plan includes a bright amber wash during “Northbound,” which made two lines hard to read on the rehearsal monitor. Jo moved those cues a little earlier where the vocal allowed it, but did not change the words or remove either line. The rehearsal monitor is smaller than the hall screen, and we do not know yet whether the side panels will be active.
3. I asked Ravi to check the file's final cue and the playback start point during the technical check on June 13. That is a request, not a report that he has tested them. If the venue asks for a fresh export after Jo adjusts the layout, I will send Ravi the new file name and ask him to replace v3 in the playback folder. Until Leena replies, I have not asked Jo to export a second layout, and Ravi still has only the current version.
4. The band's manager, Sal, requested a copy for review before the show, and I told Sal I would send the next checked version after the screen layout is known. Sal did not ask to approve the lyrics, which came from the band-approved sheet; Sal asked to review the timing and spelling of the names. I have kept the rehearsal recording in the production drive, separate from the subtitle folder, because it includes private comments before the first song. Jo has access to the subtitle folder but not to that separate recording folder, so I sent Jo the rehearsal audio through the production review link instead.

I am keeping the review notes beside the file rather than inside it, so they do not appear as audience subtitles. My latest note says that Jo should recheck the spoken introduction after the line breaks are set, because the names and thanks happen in quick succession. Jo has not made that final check yet. The next file I send to Sal will still be identified as a review copy, and I will include the version name and the screen arrangement Leena confirms. If Leena has not replied by June 10, I will tell Jo that the layout question is still open rather than treating the full-width screen as confirmed.
